property_summary: For any caller equal to the current owner, transferOwnership(newOwner) must set owner exactly to the passed newOwner; the mutant sets owner to msg.sender instead, so owner() != newOwner for any newOwner other than the caller.

property_summary: For any owner-designated caller, calling owned() must complete without reverting (a successful no-op); the mutant makes owned() always revert, violating this for every admissible caller.

For any caller address, a call to owned() succeeds only when the caller is the contract's owner; the mutant inverts the check so it succeeds for non-owners and reverts for the owner, breaking this rule.

For any caller, a call to transferOwnership by an address other than the current owner must revert so that c.owner() stays unchanged; the buggy version lets any non-owner set the owner for some fuzzed caller/newOwner.

Once the current owner transfers ownership to a, they immediately lose authority: any further transferOwnership attempt by them must revert, leaving c.owner() == a; the mutant (no onlyOwner) lets them overwrite it to b, breaking the rule for any b != a.

Any caller that is not the current owner must be unable to change ownership: transferOwnership reverts for them, so c.owner() stays the same; the mutant lets any non-owner (e.g. any nonzero address, since owner defaults to 0) overwrite the owner.

Only the current owner may change ownership: for any actor, a call to transferOwnership must revert unless that actor is the contract owner; deleting the require in the modifier lets any non-owner succeed, breaking the rule.

property_summary: For any caller, a successful call to owned() must never change the owner state variable (it is a no-op guarded by onlyOwner); the mutant violates this because owned() overwrites owner with msg.sender for some caller.

Only transferOwnership may change the owner; for any caller the result of owned() must leave the owner variable equal to the value most recently installed via transferOwnership — tightened so owned() is only ever invoked by the current owner (the admissible domain where it does not revert).

After ownership has been installed via transferOwnership, any attempt to invoke owned() (from any caller) must never change the owner away from the address explicitly installed by transferOwnership; the mutant breaks this by overwriting owner with msg.sender on successful owned() calls.

For any owner installed via transferOwnership and any caller, a call to owned() (whether it reverts for a non-owner or succeeds for the owner) must leave the owner variable equal to the address installed by transferOwnership; the mutant overwrites owner with msg.sender on successful owned() calls, breaking the rule when the caller differs from the previously installed owner.

For any owner installed via transferOwnership and any caller, a successful call to owned() must leave the owner variable equal to the address installed by transferOwnership (a non-owner's call simply reverts); the mutant's inserted `owner = msg.sender;` breaks this by overwriting the installed owner on successful owned() calls.

For any nonzero newOwner, after transferOwnership(newOwner) a call to owned() from the new owner must leave owner unchanged at newOwner; the mutant resets owner to address(0), breaking this for every nonzero newOwner.

For any nonzero newOwner set via transferOwnership (by the current owner), a subsequent authorized call to owned() by the new owner must leave ownership unchanged; the mutant's owned() resets owner to address(0), breaking this.
For every caller that is not the current owner, calling owned() must revert; the mutant removed the require so any non-owner (e.g. any address while owner is address(0)) can execute it successfully.
